metadata.title: PISA 2018 Results (Volume II): Where All Students Can Succeed

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2018 volume reports results based on the PISA international assessment design, which uses complex sampling of students within schools and schools within education systems. The reader’s guide specifies that when principals’ school questionnaire responses are presented, they are weighted so that they are proportionate to the number of 15-year-olds enrolled in the school, indicating the use of sampling/coverage weights at least for school-level reporting. The excerpt does not provide the specific student weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or any replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so the exact weighting implementation cannot be fully reconstructed from the provided text. Because this is a descriptive large-scale assessment results report (not an ML prediction paper), the appropriate “weights” are those used in the official PISA scaling and reporting pipeline; analysts should rely on the OECD/PISA database documentation for the exact weight and variance-estimation variables.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not directly handled in the provided excerpt because this document is a results volume describing equity patterns and reporting summary statistics/percentages rather than specifying an analysis pipeline that uses PV draws for a student-level predictive model. Missing data is also not described in terms of an imputation/deletion strategy for an empirical model; instead, the reader’s guide uses publication symbols (e.g., a/c/m/w) to denote categories where data do not apply, are too sparse, or are not available/withdrawn. Therefore, the PV and missing-data handling details required for an extraction of an empirical modeling strategy are not present in the supplied text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The excerpt describes PISA’s target population as 15-year-old students (aged 15 years 3 months to 16 years 2 months) who are enrolled in school and have completed at least 6 years of formal schooling, regardless of institution type, and whether full-time or part-time. It also states that the volume covers 79 countries and economies, and that B-S-J-Z (China) refers to the four participating provinces/municipalities (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang). No additional analytic subsample restrictions (e.g., specific grade bands, item/module completion filters, or exclusion rules for missing questionnaire items) are specified in the provided text; therefore, the analytic sample is treated as the full available PISA 2018 target population for the countries/economies included in the reported tables/figures.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2018 Results (Volume II) report synthesizes equity-related patterns in reading performance and related student, school, and system outcomes for 15-year-olds across 79 participating education systems. The reader’s guide clarifies that the volume reports data underlying figures in Annex B and uses standardized missing-data symbols (a/c/m/w/x) to denote categories such as not applicable, too few observations, not available, withdrawn, or data included elsewhere. The executive summary highlights descriptive benchmarks such as the OECD-average socio-economic gradient (R²) and the share of academically resilient disadvantaged students (top quarter of reading performance among disadvantaged students). It also reports equity indicators by gender and immigrant background (e.g., gender gaps in reading, prevalence of immigrant students, and differences in reading performance after accounting for socio-economic profile). Because the excerpt does not provide an explicit student-level predictive modeling pipeline, the document should be interpreted as assessment results and policy-relevant descriptive evidence rather than an ML study with reported model metrics.
